utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution wanted to raise a matter before we hear the evidence of the next witness. Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And good morning. Your Honours, just to briefly talk about the nature of the way in which Dr. Treanor's report and testimony will be tendered. In light of the extensive adjudicated facts in this case which were based upon his report and his previous testimony, we've adopted a very abbreviated approach to his reports and testimony today. I would like to place those adjudicated facts on the record. They are 6, 13, 15 through 17, 19, 30 through 33, 38, 40, 44 through 46, 52, 54 through 58, 60, 62, 69, 70 and 71, 73, 75, 76, 78, 80 through 82, 85 through 87, 99, 100, 114 to 117, 119 and 120, 122 to 127, 131, 132, 137, 144, 170, 180, 220, 223, 224, 226, 228, 231, 233 to 239, 370, 455, and 1118. Obviously, if any of these areas are challenged on cross cross-examination, we will revisit the areas of the report and documents which address those points. It is worth noting that we're taking an approach similar to the one we took with the report of Dean Manning, in which we relied on certain portions of the report, although, in this situation, for slightly different reasons. And, Your Honours, finally, I will do not do a public summary for this witness and will advise the Trial Chamber that he does have clean copies of his reports with him, and he will be bringing them into the courtroom. With that, Your Honour, we're -- I believe we're prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Treanor. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is handed out to you now. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Treanor. Mr. Treanor, will you first be examined by Ms. Bibles. You'll find her to your right. Ms. Bibles, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you to please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: My name is Patrick Joseph Treanor.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that the Court Officer bring the first page of 65 ter 13537 -- excuse me, 15573, Dr. Treanor's CV to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: As your copy of your CV appears on the screens, could you tell us whether this document was prepared before your retirement from ICTY?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm afraid this is not the correct number, 15573. Could it be 13573?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe this document was prepared before my retirement.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't have a document before me yet, but what is the right number? There we are.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, this is number document number 13573.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. Treanor answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When did you retire?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: I retired at the end of 2009.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Since your retirement, have you reviewed any documents which may have come in to the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: You mean new documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: New documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And since this transcript was -- or excuse me, this CV was prepared, you've testified in the case of Prosecutor versus Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would tender 65 ter 13573 at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 13573 receives number P3001 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3001 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review excerpts from your testimony in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the transcript accurately reflects your testimony at that time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, the portion of the transcript that I recently reviewed does.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Is there anything that you would add to the transcript that you reviewed regarding your reports?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: No, the portion of the transcript that I reviewed related to the methodology that I used in writing my reports. I would only add to state explicitly, that I was the -- the person ultimately responsible for everything that went into the report. I decided what went into the reports based on my expert opinion, and that I was careful in my methodology to reference by footnote virtually every statement or at least every paragraph in the report so that the documents were allowed to speak for themselves and it was made clear which documents were speaking in regard to particular statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If you were asked today about the substance of your testimony aside from these two additions -- or with these two additions, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Having taken the solemn declaration, do you affirm the truthfulness and accuracy of your testimony in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 30425 which are the excerpts of testimony of Dr. Treanor in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30425 receives number P3002, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When you were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I invite both speakers not to overlap, but to pause between question and answer and the next question. It's very important because the last answer was missing. The "yes" after line 10 and 11 of page 5, that you affirmed the truthfulness and accuracy of your testimony in the Karadzic case, and the witness said "yes."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: When you're reviewing documents for the purposes of your research, you work from the English translation or from the original documents?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: I worked from the original B/C/S versions of the documents, as did most of the other members of my team.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: To ask one more question in addition to those asked in the Karadzic case regarding your selection of documents, could you describe for us how you assess the value of a historical source when selecting materials for inclusion in your reports?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: I considered to the most value sources the various types of documents that were generated by the -- the party under consideration in a given report, in the case of these reports they would be the Bosnian Serb leadership, so we focused on collecting and analysing documents produced by the highest level, political; that is, political party organisations and state organisations of the Bosnian Serbs. Those are the -- the primary and most important sources that I used, and as I say we made a very intensive methodical search for these documents in an attempt to acquire them and analyse them and eventually utilise them in these reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now to your report, "The Bosnian Serb Leadership 1990 to 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'd ask that 65 ter 02881 be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We see this report signed by you in 2002. Can you tell us the scope and purpose of this report.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: The purpose of this report was to outline the origins and developments of the principal political structures that were developed by the Bosnian Serbs. That is, the -- the Serbian Democratic Party and its -- its organs, and the principal organs of the Republika Srpska that they -- the Bosnian Serb leadership eventually founded. It deals with the period commencing in approximately 1990 and ending at the -- the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Are there any limitations or considerations we should be aware of in reviewing this report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't say so. The documentation that we had available at that time offered a fairly complete picture of -- of those developments, and any documents that I saw after that basically only tended to confirm the -- the main outlines of the report. There are certainly many details that could be filled in. But in general terms, the -- the main thrust of the report and the various sections on the party and the state organs are -- have held up very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd next like to turn to 65 ter 11849, the report Bosnian report titled: "The Bosnian Serb leadership: 1993 to 1995, addendum to the Bosnian Serb leadership." Could you please describe how the contents of the report we see on the screen relate to your 2002 report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, this report is -- is basically a continuation of the previous report. It continues the -- the stories, if you will, that were told in the original report about the -- the SDS and the -- the various organs of the Bosnian Serb republic forward until the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask for both of these reports to be marked for identification, pending the completion of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, numbers to be assigned?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 02881 receives number P3003. And document 11849 receives number P3004, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I'd like to begin by discussing the Assembly of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your report details that the Bosnian Serb Assembly was created by the decision of the SDS Deputies Club on 24 October 1991. Could you very briefly describe what the SDS Deputies Club was?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, the -- the SDS Deputies Club was one of the several Deputies Clubs in the Assembly of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Each political party had -- there was represented in the assembly, organised what they -- in their terminology call a club, in the US we call that a party caucus, in which the members -- the delegates to the assembly who are members of that party met and discussed what positions they would take on matters before the assembly. So the Deputies Club of the Serbian Democratic Party consisted of 60-odd members. I believe that's -- the details are given in the report. It also included one member of the -- the SPO, the Serbian Movement for Renewal, they had one delegate and he met with their club. That encompassed almost all of the members of the assembly who were of Serbian nationality. I think there were five or six members of Serbian nationality who were not members of the club, but the SDS Deputies Club included almost all of the Serbian members of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, in order to avoid any confusion, the transcript may not be entirely clear as what I said in relation to P3003 and P3004. Both are marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, if the Court Officer could bring 65 ter 11284, which is a transcript of the session of the SDS Deputies Club and founding the assembly, to our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: While this document is coming to our screen, I'll ask you whether prior to this date in October of 1991 was there an openly separate governing body of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, there was no separate governing body of the Bosnian Serbs on the -- at the centre on the -- central level in Bosnia and Herzegovina. There -- there had been established on the regional level a certain -- or referred to as autonomous regions or districts by the -- under the auspices of the SDS which encompassed certain municipalities in various regions of the country, but at the central in Sarajevo at the -- the -- the level of the republican government, there was no separate Serbian institution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could -- could you tell us what the significance is of the decision that is reflected in the transcripts for which we have the first page on our screens.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, basically what occurred at this session was the foundation of a separate assembly for the Bosnian Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina by the SDS Deputies Club. That is -- that new Serbian Assembly included all the members of the Deputies Club and other Serbian delegates to -- or deputies to the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were invited to attend to join as well. All of the members, in other words, were -- had been elected as deputies to the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and at the session, however, they declared that they would have their own Serbian Assembly which would be the -- the highest law-giving body for the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They would only recognise such decisions that were taken by the regularly constituted governing bodies in Bosnia and Herzegovina if the Serbian Assembly agreed to them. And at this session they elected, Momcilo Krajisnik to be the president of their assembly, and he was also the president of the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And I would point out that the members of this Serbian Assembly continued to attend such sessions of the regular assembly as -- as they saw fit to, and Momcilo Krajisnik continued to act as the president of that assembly as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 11248.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it 248 or 284?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You called it 284 earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we have on our screen, Madam Registrar, could you please repeat the 65 ter number and then assign a...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document on screen which is 11284 receives number P3005, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3005 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: On 9 January 1992, this assembly adopted a declaration that you describe in paragraph 177 of your 2002 report as being: "Final step in a gradual buildup of a separate state entity in Bosnia and Herzegovina." I'd like to turn to that document and ask a couple of questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I would ask that 65 ter 03209, the declaration on the proclamation of the Republic of the Serbian people of Bosnia and Herzegovina be brought to our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Are we looking at the declaration that you described in paragraph 177 here?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, now if we could go to page 2 in both B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: We see under Article 3, the declaration states that: "Territorial delimitation with political communities of other peoples in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as the solution of other mutual rights and obligations, shall be performed peacefully and consensually. Ethnic, historical, league, cultural, economic, geographical communications, and other significant criteria will be taken into account, and the principles and rules of international law will be observed." The reference in Article 3 to the peaceful manner seems contrary to much of the public rhetoric heard from the Bosnian Serb leadership in October and November of 1991. Is there a contextual explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, at -- at this time, this time being the end of 1991, beginning of 1992, while the Bosnian Serbs were establishing their -- their own institutions, the assembly, the end of December, we've seen the foundation of the assembly at the end of December, they formed a council of ministers. And with this declaration they have stated that they were going to have a separate territory within Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's why I call it the final step, although there were other steps taken after this to put flesh on the bones that they had created. But they were conducting negotiations with the -- the other two main political parties in Bosnia-Herzegovina; that is, the HDZ, the Croatian Democratic Union, and the SDA, the Party for Democratic Action which a party of the Bosnian Muslims. They were negotiating with those parties with a view to the -- about the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina and its internal structure and its relationship to the -- what was still the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And those negotiations in -- in January 1992 were about to recommence under the auspices of the European union in the person of Jose Cutileiro of Portugal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 03209.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03209 receives P3006, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph of your report, paragraph 178, you list several particularly important pieces of legislation from the assembly. Let's first turn to the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have the first page of 65 ter 07187 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Looking at the first page, is this the constitution described in your report?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could stay on page 1 in the B/C/S -- or in the original language and go to page 2 in English. And looking Articles 1 and 2, it -- when we look at Article 1, we see that it identifies that the Serbian republic is the state of the Serb people. And in Article 2 we see that it sets out territory. "The territory of the republic consist of Serb autonomous regions, municipalities, and other Serb ethnic entity, including the regions in which genocide was committed against the Serb people in the Second World War." Based on your research and experience in this field, did these criteria for the establishment of the Serbian state within Bosnia and Herzegovina remain constant during the war?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: In general terms, yes. This -- this article puts forward a -- a -- some definition of -- of the territory that they wanted to include within their republic as opposed to the January declaration which merely stated that there would be a territory and that it would be defined in negotiations with the other parties based on various criteria. Here, they're setting out what, in their view, those territories should consist of. I would have to mention, however, that the Autonomous Districts were in fact abolished by amendment to this constitution in September 1992 by which time the territories of those autonomous republics had been included within the republic, but -- the republic at that time in September 1992, sort of centralised, if you will, and the autonomous districts themselves were abolished. But the -- with that minor exception, the -- the principle remained the same. The Bosnian Serbs want those territories which had -- which had -- had been historically Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 07187.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 07187 receives number P3007, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You also list the Law on National Defence as being significant.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could have the first page of 65 ter 03225 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what date the National Defence Act was enacted?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: It was enacted on February 28th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And what was the effective date?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: It was - I think in terms of the last article of this law - it was to come into effect eight days after it was published in the Official Gazette, and the date of publication we say is 23 March 1992, so it would have come into effect on the 31st of March, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you put these dates into context with the other events at the time?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned the negotiations which were going on. They were still going on at this time. However, the -- during that period, the -- the Bosnian Serb leadership continued to develop their own state within Bosnia and Herzegovina, including the adoption of the constitution and this law and other laws. And while negotiations were going on in March, there was much discussion in the Bosnian Serb Assembly about establishing control on the ground, and this law and some of the other laws were published on the 23rd of March. While the negotiations were still going on, and given the fact that it stated that they would come into operation, in fact, eight days after the publication, we can conclude that by the 23rd of March, before the negotiations had -- had concluded, they had already decided that they were going to activate -- in fact, activate their own state institutions as of the end of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could go to page 5 in the original language and page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'll direct your attention to Articles 5 and 6. Could you describe for us the significance of Articles 5 and 6 of this National Defence Act?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, Article 5 describes the role of the National Assembly in the national defence structure of the Bosnian Serb republic. I would point out the -- the portion at the end of the paragraph where it -- says that the Assembly would appoint the commander of the Territorial Defence of the republic in keeping with the proposals submitted by the president. And article 6 deals with the -- the role of the president of the republic in the Bosnian Serb -- in the -- in the defence system of the Bosnian Serb republic. And I might point out there the portions in which it -- Article 6 says that the president shall supervise the Territorial Defence both in peace and war-time. I think the word "supervised" might be better translated as "control." And at the end of the paragraph, it speaks about the president's relationship to the police, where it says at the end of that paragraph in English: "He shall issue orders for the utilisation of the police in case of a state of war, imminent threat of war, and other emergencies ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: At some point in time, before the 12th of May of 1992, was an imminent state of war declared?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes. The imminent threat of war was declared in -- in the -- in a decision signed by the two acting presidents of the Bosnian Serb republic on the 15th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, we have a witness who works on the basis of the original language and says that the translation he sees before him is not the one he would. Now, the witness is not a translator, but, nevertheless, since he worked from the original, would you please take care that, at least the issue whether it should be "supervised" or "control" Territorial Defence will be reviewed and to report what CLSS thinks about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And perhaps if the witness could explain why he disagrees with our official translation, we would appreciate that, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it linguistically that you or is it on the basis of your understanding on the role of the president that you made this observation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I believe the word in Serbo-Croatian is "ubukovode" which comes -- is derived from the word for "hand." It's frequently translated as -- as control, manage -- or manage. "Supervise" to me means a -- a little bit more distant relationship, kind of monitoring rather than actually controlling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Bibles, I think it's worthwhile to submit it perhaps again to CLSS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, and I would tender 65 ter 03225, acknowledging that we may mark it for identification pending this translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03225 receives number P3008, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3008 is marked for identification pending verification of the translation of Article 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You also describe in several sections of your report the creation of parallel municipal structures over which the Bosnian Serb leadership gives direction. I'd like to turn an example of that. If we could go to the first page of 65 ter 03228, a dispatch from the deputy minister of the interior. Could you tell us briefly who signed this document.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: This document is signed by Momcilo Mandic who was an assistant minister for internal affairs in the Ministry of Internal affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: What does this document direct?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, this document, which was sent out to basically all members of the ministry, irrespective of their ethnicity, informing them that the -- pursuant to decisions taken by the Bosnian Serb Assembly that as of the 1st of April, 1992, there would be an separate Serbian Ministry of Internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And could you tell us the importance of the manner in which this announcement was made?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I think it's important in -- in relation to the timing, which is, I indicated, about -- in connection with the publication of the law which was published while negotiations were going on and specifying that the laws would come into effect eight days later. And this is, in fact, sent out on the eighth day, I believe, or certainly thereabouts. So it's in close conformity with that. And this document, although perhaps it doesn't -- it doesn't look that way, is a rather public step. That is, it went to everyone -- everyone in the ministry irrespective of ethnicity. So it is a unilateral step taken by Bosnian Serb leaders as were the other steps we've discussed. The January declaration, the formation of the assembly, and their laws, they were all -- these were all steps which were taken unilaterally. However, they were taken very publicly, and as I said, this is as far as the ministry was concerned is virtually a public document. So they were very open about their intentions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 03228.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03228 receives number P3009, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: On the 12th of May, 1992, the assembly created the Army of Republika Srpska. I'd like to show you a document with the same date and ask you to comment on the impact of the changes it brings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: If we could see the first page of 65 ter 03261, the decision on the promulgation of amendments 1 through 4 to the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what these amendments meant for the military and other armed forces.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at the amendments. Basically these amendments transform the Territorial Defence organisation which was mentioned in the original February constitution of the Bosnian Serb republic into an army. The Territorial Defence organisation was part of the -- the Yugoslav defence structure and was a military force which was appropriate to the various -- to the republics which were constituents of the SFRY. The Bosnian Serb republic considered itself to be a -- one of those constituent parts. In fact, technically it always considered itself to be part of the -- the federal state of Yugoslavia which is specified in Article 3 of their constitution I believe. However, in fact, they -- they declared their independence on the -- I believe it was the 6th of April, 1992, at a session of the assembly, and these amendments to the constitution are -- are reflective of a -- a type of military organisation more appropriate to an independent state rather than one that was going to be functioning as -- as simply part of the -- the -- the Territorial Defence organisation of -- of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 03261.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03261 receives number P3010, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Before we shift our attention to the Presidency, I'd like you to reflect briefly on the leadership abilities of Krajisnik in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, Momcilo Krajisnik was elected to the Assembly of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1990 as an SDS candidate. He subsequently became a member of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party, and as we've seen was elected president of -- of the Bosnian Serb Assembly. He seems to have been, based on the transcripts of that assembly, a very strong leader. He led the assembly sessions in a very efficient manner, and he -- he -- he was a -- a leader of the assembly more -- more in the American model than perhaps the British model. He was very a very political person, and he advocated certain positions, and he usually got what he wanted out of the assembly. They usually adopted positions that -- that he did favour. Not that there was frequently, quite frankly, great differences of opinion within the assembly. But he was a strong leader and he got things through the assembly in a very efficient manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Can you comment just briefly on his relationship with Radovan Karadzic in -- in getting things through the assembly?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, Radovan Karadzic was the -- the leader -- the president of the Serbian Democratic Party, and he -- he did not occupy any official position, any government-type position either within the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina or in the Bosnian Serb republic until -- until May 1992. So during the period when the, say, when the Bosnian Serb Assembly was formed and during its early sessions, Momcilo Krajisnik was the one that ran the sessions, and -- and moved -- moved the agenda forward, and he did that in -- in agreement with the -- with Radovan -- in political agreement with Radovan Karadzic and the -- as far as we know, with the rest of the Main Board of the Serbian Democratic Party. Their close co-operation in the establishment of the Bosnian Serb institutions, and indeed the continuation of those institutions until the end of 1995, was very important. They formed a united political front which made the Bosnian Serb leadership very strong both internally and vis-à-vis the -- the other parties in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and indeed beyond the boundaries of Bosnia-Herzegovina, most especially perhaps the Serbian leadership in Belgrade. Slobodan Milosevic, who was the president of Serbia at this time, was able to use political differences, say, among the Croatian Serbs who had established similar institutions of their own within Croatia. He was able to use differences between, say -- or precisely between the presidents of the Croatian Serbs and the -- the leader of their assembly in order to, in fact, remove Milan Babic who was the early president of the -- the Croatian Serbs. So this type of political manoeuvring was not possible vis-à-vis the Bosnian Serb leadership in view of, as I say, their strong political unity which was -- the basis of which was the close co-operation between Radovan Karadzic and Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning now to the composition of the Presidency, could you tell us who made up the Presidency as of the 12th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: On the 12th May of 1992, the constitutional law, which was passed on the 28th of February, 1992, at the same time as the constitution, which contained various transitional provisions, in -- in connection with the implementation of that constitution was amended, and the -- the -- the powers of the president of the republic, which is the -- the organ specified in the -- in the constitution as of the 12th of March -- 12th of May, 1992, were to be exercised pursuant to the amendments of the constitutional law on that date by a three-member Presidency. The assembly elected the three members to that Presidency on that date, and they elected Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic, who had been the Serbian members of the joint Presidency of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and they had been elected with SDS support. And they had been the acting presidents of the Serbian republic. And the third member elected by the assembly was Dr. Radovan Karadzic. So this was his first formal official high-level position in the Bosnian Serb republic. And on that date, the -- the three members of the Presidency elected Radovan Karadzic to be the -- the chairman or president of -- of that Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I note that it is both time and a -- perhaps a good location to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is, Ms. Bibles. Could you tell us whether you're on track as far as time is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Very much so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that you would need how much time after the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we estimated an hour and a half total. I believe we've used 50 minutes at this point. I will be considerably less than -- than an hour and a half in total.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could -- Mr. Treanor, we'd like to take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you describe for us the changes made to the Presidency on the 1st of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, on the 1st of June, the constitutional law that I referred to earlier was amended yet again to establish a five-member Presidency. The -- the three-member Presidency was expanded with the addition of the president of the assembly, Momcilo Krajisnik, and the prime minister Branko Djeric.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Turning to some of the specifics of the powers of the Presidency, in paragraph 238 of your report, you advise that in addition to the specified powers of the Presidency, that the overwhelming SDS majority in the assembly meant that the Presidency also had de facto political control over the government. Was this political situation true throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes. The SDS continued to -- to dominate the assembly. The membership of the assembly was basically stable with a few additions and subtractions over the years. But the same SDS membership was in place, Radovan Karadzic remained the president of the party. Members of the party were obliged to follow party policy. The -- the prime ministers, Branko Djeric had been an SDS appointee, if you will, originally in the government of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, after him the prime ministers, I think they were all members of the Main Board of the SDS. So the SDS had a lock on -- on the assembly of the government and the Presidency. And of course in the person of Radovan Karadzic, he himself was in a position to politically control all of those actors, and he actively used his party powers to do so. Later on 1994, 1995, we see in the addendum certain members of the assembly were expelled for breaking with SDS policy and since they had -- they were members of the SDS and had been elected as SDS representatives, they were removed from the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: You further explain in your report that the formal powers of the Presidency set out in Article 80 of the constitution were also frequently enhanced by the use of the emergency provision of the constitution set out in Article 81, paragraph 2. I'd like to now focus on one of the laws passed under this provision.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could see the first page of the Law of the Army at 65 ter 03285.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain what this Law of the Army sets out?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: This law sets out the internal organisation of the Army of the Serbian republic and specifies the competences and the duties of the various members of the armed forces -- of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And if we could turn to, I believe, it's page 2 in both versions to focus on Article 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Could you read for us the powers given to the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to read from the English for the sake of simplicity, and I can read it better on the screen. As -- Article 10: "The commander of the Main Staff shall in compliance with the establishment of the army and decisions of the president of the republic: "1, Outline the plan of conscription, replenishment, and numerical disposition of conscripts in the army --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, could you please read a bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. "2, Outline plans for the training and advancement of the active and reserve superior officers, the army needs. "3, Outline annual plans of education and training for the active and reserve superior officers at military academies for the needs of the army. "4, Ensure co-ordination of replenishment for the army. "5, Inspect combat readiness of the army. "6, Perform other duties falling within his competence by law relevant to replenishment of the army with conscripts and registered materiel."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 03285.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 03285 receives number P3011, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Finally, your report details the development --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, do you have any follow-up questions on this article?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I do not. I'm sorry, we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you assume that the Chamber was unable to read a -- Article 10?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: I merely wanted to highlight the role of the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are other ways in doing that rather than to just ask a witness to read the text, which the Chamber can read as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your report details the development of the SDS as a political party and how it transforms the leadership and the government of the Republika Srpska. I'd ask you to briefly go through some of the individuals as I name them and briefly describe their role and their importance to the Bosnian Serb leadership. The first would be Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, Radovan Karadzic, as I mentioned earlier, was the president of the Serbian Democratic Party. He was elected president at its first assembly in -- in 1990. He continued to be president of the party until the -- until the end of 1995 and beyond. And as the leader of the party, he was the dominant figure in establishing the -- the policy of the party. He had exercised certain emergency powers in that respect under the statutes of the party. He -- he -- was -- was -- did not occupy a position in the -- in the governing structures of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina as did the -- the leaders of the other political parties, that they did occupy positions within that government. He did not run for any office. However, as the -- the leader of the party, of the SDS, he was -- played a very important role in the establishment of the separate institutions for the Bosnian Serbs, as we've seen. We mentioned the -- the regions, the assembly, the -- the republic itself, and he did come to occupy a -- a -- an informal position -- well, not informal but not a constitutional position, shortly after the -- the outbreak of the conflict in early April 1992 with the establishment of the -- the national -- so-called national security council of the Bosnian Serbs, which was a body established by the assembly in -- on 27th of March, 1992. He, in fact, acted as the chairman of that National Security Council which operated as sort of a national-level Crisis Staff in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Other members were minister of internal affairs, for instance, minister of defence, and the two acting presidents in whose names its decisions were issued. Then on May 12 we see him elected, actually elected by the assembly as a member of the Presidency. This is it -- his first formal constitutional position in the republic. He continued in the -- the expanded Presidency, and then on the -- I believe it was the 17th of December, 1992, he was elected the single president of the Bosnian Serb republic with -- along with two vice-presidents, Biljana Plavsic and Nikola Koljevic. And he continued in that position until the -- the end of 1995 and beyond.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And I'd like to next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Bibles, could I just revisit for a second the Law of the Army, the Law on the Army you just tendered, which was admitted. Now I see that it's a 55-page document of which I think Article 10 was read without any further questions. As I explained before, the Chamber, if something is in evidence, takes that seriously. So, therefore, do you want us to read the remaining 54 pages and two or three articles as well and what to do with that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a document I perhaps could have tendered from the bar table. It is a significant document with respect to the army and to the trial in this case with respect to how it functioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, my --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And that would be the purpose of introducing the entire document, because we -- this is one that will be used as the trial progresses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the trial will not progress much more as far as the Prosecution's case is concerned. And if I read that there are nice chapters about applications after you finish your education, what to do with compensation if are you -- is that all that we really have to pay attention to it? Or is it rather that you have certain portions of that law which are specifically relevant and why not then just reduce the evidence to those portions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. For the last two minutes, neither Mr. Mladic nor I have been receive any B/C/S interpretation on channel 6. I believe there may be a technical problem. So we weren't able to follow this part of the discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see if there's any ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems to be fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then perhaps I briefly repeat what we did over the last two minutes. After the witness had answered the last question put to him by Ms. Bibles, I inquired as to whether we needed the whole of the Law on the Army into evidence, or whether Ms. Bibles could have made -- have chosen excerpts of direct relevance to the case. Ms. Bibles, would you give it some thought on whether you really need all the -- all the chapters and paragraphs of that legislation so that the Chamber and it's a staff will have to go through it, or rather that you would select the most relevant portions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll consult with Mr. Stojanovic on that process as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we hear from you, well, let's say later this week so that we can revisit what should be admitted or whether there's a -- excerpts which could replace the entirety of the text of the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: In proceeding on, could you very briefly describe the role of Ms. Plavsic during the war.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, Biljana Plavsic was the SDS candidate -- an SDS candidate for the Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina at the elections in -- in 1990, along with Nikola Koljevic. I can mention him along the way, perhaps, for the sake of efficiency. They were both elected and served in that Presidency in 1991 and in that capacity advocated the positions of the Serbian Democratic Party. When the -- they -- they attended the opening session of the -- of the assembly in October and -- and later sessions, and they -- they played a very important role in the establishment of the central institutions of the Bosnian Serb republic but becoming its acting presidents under the constitution and the constitutional law of February 1992, that was very important because they had been elected to the Presidency. Therefore, like the members of the Bosnian Serb Assembly, they -- they had a -- an independent legitimacy that they say had been endorsed by the voters, and that lent a legitimacy to the -- to the new Bosnian Serb structures. And they both continued to be members of the Presidency throughout 1992, equal members, I might add, with the other members. The five-member Presidency did establish at one of its sessions certain divisions of powers among the members, certain areas that they would pay particular attention to, but they were all jointly responsible for the exercising the powers of the president of the republic as such. And at the end of December 1992, they were both elected vice-presidents and continued in those positions until the end of 1995 and continued to support the Bosnian Serb efforts, of course, and to lend their legitimacy to its Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: And, finally, how effective was the Bosnian Serb leadership in accomplishing the goal of ethnic separation within Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1991 to the end of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I would say that the -- the Bosnian Serb leadership was -- was very effective in that respect. One of its principle goals right from the beginning of the foundation of the SDS was the exercise of -- of more direct authority by Bosnian Serb leaders, Bosnian Serb officials, in the parts of the country populated by Serbs. This is a process that can, in shorthand, be described as regionalisation, but it also included the municipal level. The -- in certain cases one has to redraw boundaries of municipalities so they would be more Serbian, and then have those municipalities united in regions. Now, if they wanted that irrespective of whether Bosnia-Herzegovina remained within Yugoslavia or not, their other main goal was, of course, to keep Bosnia-Herzegovina within Yugoslavia. To -- to keep -- to keep it short, they were not successful in that -- in that second goal, in keeping the -- the Serbs within Bosnia and Herzegovina -- Bosnia-Herzegovina within Yugoslavia, but they were successful in -- in effect partitioning Bosnia-Herzegovina, the establishment of their independent institutions -- of their separate institutions beginning with the assembly, was extremely important that process because it attracted the attention of the international community to the position of the Bosnian Serbs within Bosnia. They -- the assembly, in letters signed by Momcilo Krajisnik, sent letters to the EU and international negotiators, international bodies making them aware of the desire of the Bosnian Serbs to remain within Yugoslavia and to have a their own institutions, et cetera, and the international community basically paid heed to that and negotiations in 1992 and later proceeded on the basis of having a separate Bosnian Serb entity within Bosnia-Herzegovina which was something that many people had said was impossible. You can't partition Bosnia, and they in fact managed to do so and get the international community to recognise that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: This concludes my examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. Mr. Stojanovic, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Treanor? Mr. Treanor, you will be cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Stojanovic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Professor. First of all, I'd start with the a general question which would be a lead-up to some of the documents I'll rely on. In parallel with conducting your analysis of the documents produced by the political leadership of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as assembly decisions of the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you also analyse such documents put forth by the parties' representative of the Muslim and Croat population in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, it was the responsibility of my team to analyse the -- the structures of all the parties to the conflict in the former Yugoslavia. And we did so. My particular personal area of -- of expertise right from the beginning of my employ at ICTY was in fact the Bosnian Serbs. But I -- I personally did also do -- do some work in relation to the -- the other parties, and members of my team were assigned to -- to work on all of those parties and, in many cases, we produced reports similar to the ones under consideration today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While applying your analytical and methodological approach to the issue you dealt with, did you try to establish any chronological causality between the decisions of the political and assembly leadership of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina with the decisions issued by the political and assembly leadership of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I think we certainly established the chronology of those decisions. I -- I wouldn't perhaps use the word "causality" as something which I brought -- would have brought out as being to a certain extent speculative.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I will actually ask you as one of my main points: In the decisions produced by the two leaderships, is there a cause and effect principle in place or examples of inviting the issue of certain decisions, or did your analysis prove that there wasn't any such connection?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure what you mean by two leaderships. There were, generally speaking, three leaderships: Serbian, Muslim, and Croatian. They all had -- they had different aspirations which was -- therein lies the problem. So they all sort of fed off of each other to a certain extent, but they -- they -- they had their -- their own aspirations -- and -- and those aspirations were to a greater or lesser extent shared by other actors in the Yugoslav region; namely, in Croatia and in the -- what was left of the -- what became the FRY. Well, let me just leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, in your view and according to your analysis, up to what moment in time did Bosnia-Herzegovina remain, de facto and de jure, as part of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I -- I think maybe I can deal with the de facto part better than de jure part, not being a legal expert. But it -- it -- it would seem to me that certainly by the -- the fall of -- of 1991, that Bosnia and Herzegovina was -- was basically acting as a -- a separate entity from the -- from the Federation. And, indeed, it -- it was being treated on -- on a different -- on a separate basis by the international community; that is, they organised connections with Bosnia in particular, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your analysis, did you deal with the issue of the constitutional and legal regulation of the status of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a constituent part of the SFRY, as well as the constitutional path, so to speak, taken by Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I've looked at those issues, certainly, and I have produced other reports as well. I'm not -- in which those issues perhaps are better -- better reflected than -- than they are in -- in these two reports, which deal with -- mostly with the internal structures of the Bosnian Serb republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let's jointly take a look at a document. That would be the constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia dated 25th of February, 1974.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 65 ter document 07482. B/C/S page 7; English page 18, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to be shown, Professor, as per the constitution of the SFRY, did the sovereignty derive from territory or from peoples?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, again, I'm not a constitutional expert, and -- and I would -- could only point to certain articles in the constitution and what they say. And if you'd like to direct me to that, I'd be pleased. But I -- I generally speak and write on the basis of particular documents and not by -- not by -- by memory. I think that -- you know, we got to get to look at relevant articles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if you want the witness to further look at relevant articles of the constitution of the SFRY --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would you please keep in mind that the witness now twice said that he is not a legal expert. And would you also not forget that the core of this case is not about who was right or wrong in seeking independence or to stay within the federal system but that this case is -- the core of the case is elsewhere. Would you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'll try to keep this as brief as possible. But it seems to me that this expertise is part and parcel of an analysis of constitutional matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Professor, Article 3, could you please take a look at it. This is the constitution of the then-SFRY. It says here: "The socialist republics, including Bosnia-Herzegovina, are states based on the sovereignty of the people and the power of and self-management by the working class and all working people and are socialist self-managing democratic communities of the working people and citizens and of nations and nationalities having equal rights." Would this jog your memory as to whether or not the sovereignty of the republics is based on the sovereignty of the peoples living in those republics or not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: That's what the article says in general terms. I'm sorry, which constitution is this? Is this the constitution of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was introduced by Mr. Stojanovic as the constitution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, 25th of February, 1974.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, my question relates to the fact that Article 3, in fact, says the socialist republic or a socialist republic is a state. The plural is not used. So I'm not sure what -- what the -- the reference is to when it says "socialist republic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we may have a translation issue here because the English says: "The socialist republics are states based upon ...," and you say in the original text is singular Mr. Treanor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And of course they don't have articles in Serbo-Croatian, so the -- if the reference is in fact a general one to all the socialist republics of the federation, then its translation in the plural would be appropriate. But again, I didn't -- I lost sight of which constitution this was and I saw in the singular there, whereas it's in the plural in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: But the crux of the matter is this. This is the SFRY constitution. This is the provision of Article 3 of that constitution. And my question is deriving from this constitutional definition, and we are going to deal with the constitution of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina later, is it correct what I put forward, is that each republic within the SFRY was a state based on the sovereignty of the people living in it? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, in general terms, that's correct. Again, there's some linguistic problems here in -- in -- Serbo-Croatian in writing it -- the -- the genitive singular and the genitive plural are the same. So is -- just on the face of it, it's difficult to say whether it's based on the sovereignty of the "people" or the "peoples," meaning to say, the Serbian people, the Muslim people, the Croatian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can specify that by perusing the constitution of the BH. But I think I got your answer. Let's now focus on Article 5 of the then-constitution of the SFRY. And to ask me -- ask you whether you will agree with me that in practical terms as early as in 1991, there was no possibility of changing the territories of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia without applying the procedure that has been laid down in that constitution?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, if -- if you're telling me the constitution lay down a procedure, I would have to agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at paragraph 2, Article 5, of the constitution of the SFRY. When it comes to procedures, it states, inter alia: "The territory of a republic cannot be changed without the consent of that republic and the territory of an autonomous province cannot be changed without the consent of that autonomous province. Furthermore, borders of the SFRY cannot be changed without the consent of all republics and autonomous provinces." My question to you is: Could you please tell me whether this provision of Article 5 of the constitution of the SFRY was valid with respect to all republics of the SFRY in 1991?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I'm certainly under the impression that -- that -- that this remained in force, technically. However, there have been certain developments which -- on the ground which subverted it, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Professor. And this is why we are here. Now let's take a look at 65 ter document 17211. 17211. That's the constitution of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Could we please focus on Articles 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, and perhaps it should be on our screens, what do you want to do with the 1974 constitution, which you [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we prepared to tender it into evidence because we prepared only the relevant sections. But I'm going to revisit Article 5 later on and then propose for it to be tendered. If you'd like it tendered it right now, then I will be guided by your will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. As a matter of fact, it would be appreciated in you would make excerpt -- if you would select the relevant portions of it so that we don't have to study by heart the 129 pages uploaded. And I also would appreciate there was some issue about whether -- what constitution this was, how it was translated. I see that it was uploaded from apparently a book called the constitution of the -- constitutions of the countries of the world. Now, whether this is the 1974 constitution, yes or no, seems not to appear clearly from the text you have uploaded, so why not take official texts, if they are available in translation as well, and look at the translation issues, as well, before you seek portions or excerpts to be admitted. We leave it, at this moment, as it is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at items 1, 2, and 3 of the constitution of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we earlier were struggling with the English translation of the 1974 constitution. The resolution of such problems, however, is not to present no translation at all because, I do understand, that English is not uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I could see, and as far as we were given from the -- by the Prosecution, this would be that document, and this is the official translation that we received from the Prosecution. If this is a problem, we will sort it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we have in e-court is English ERN numbers, but Madam Registrar tells me that the English version, it may well exist, but was not uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the document we have on our screen at this moment is in B/C/S. Or we have -- well, first of all, the documents, on the second page gives us a lot of handwriting in numbers. And all I see after that, there -- and also the last page of the document, page 288, is full with nicely written calculations, and I do not see any English text anywhere. I see nice indexes to it. If you want to us pay attention to a constitution, then upload it in two languages and without all kind of irrelevant additions. Or do you really want us to read through 30 or 40 pages of indexes?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. If you wish me to circumvent this issue, I can try to do so, try to extract myself from this situation by putting certain questions to the witness without dealing with legal text.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Professor, would you say that I'm right when I say that the constitution of SFRY BiH, which was in effect in 1991, it was in force then, guaranteed the equality of peoples and nationalities of the peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: I believe that's correct in general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you say I'm right when I said that the Serbs, Croats, and the Muslim, as well as members of other peoples and nationalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina were those who constituted the constituent nations and peoples of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's take a look, please, at 65 ter 15207. That would be an amendment, amendment 69 to the constitution of the Bosnia-Herzegovina constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You dealt with it in your report yourself, dated 31st of July, 1990. And ow let's take a look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before you go to that, can we just check something here. If you look at page 41, line 5, you are transcribed as referring to the constitution of the SFRY BiH. I thought you were referring to the constitution of the BiH; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you. Not SFRY but Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Thank you for your kind assistance. For the benefit of the transcript, page 41, line 5, not "constitution of the SFRY" but "SRBiH." With your permission, I would like to ask the professor as follows.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's take a look at this amendment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you also assist us in taking us to the relevant paragraph in the report, of which we do not even know which one, but so that we know what portion of the report you referred to when you said the witness dealt with this constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honours, I'll try to find that footnote. It presently eludes me, but I will get back to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it you want to ask questions in that context. So, therefore, for us to follow the evidence, it would be extremely helpful to know where to look in the report. We even could consider to take the break five minutes early so that you could find it and then enable the Chamber to follow the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a second or two, that would be ... well, Professor dealt with the amendments in -- in paragraph 252, which concerns certain amendments to the constitution of the Republika Srpska. And later on, let me find reference to the amendments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I can't, then I would ask the Professor whether you dealt with amendments to the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina dated 1990 that we have on our screens here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which report, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The -- P3003.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the first report or the -- first report. And you refer us to paragraph 252, where I have some problems in -- because I wonder whether it contains a paragraph 252 at all. Because, as far as I'm aware of, paragraph 178 is the last one. Or are you referring to footnote 252? We could then look for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I'm referring to paragraph 252 of the report, which now bears the indication P3003, if I noted it down correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see whether I have the -- yes. I am -- I made a mistake, Mr. Stojanovic. I looked at the addendum rather than to the original report. Apologies for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me, Your Honours, I'm going to ask questions. This does not refer to this amendment but others, and this is why I sought your leave to ask the professor --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- whether he'd encountered this amendment which we see on our screens?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, I am familiar with this amendment, yes. I don't know where it may be mentioned in -- in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Not in this part. And this is why I wanted us to focus on this portion. We have it in the e-court system. Let's take a look at paragraph 2, item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will be the last paragraph of the English version, Your Honours. That's 65 ter 15207. 1-5-2-0-7.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It states, Professor, let me remind you, 31st of July, 1990. [As read] "It is prohibited to organise political activities geared towards change of the constitutional legal order to jeopardize territorial integrity and independence of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, all the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Socialist Federal Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Would you agree if I said that this constitutional amendment adopted on the 31st of July, 1990, it explicitly forbids, prohibits political activities against territorial integrity of the SFRY as a country?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to focus your attention to the chronology of events. Let's retrieve from the e-court Exhibit P303, P303, paragraph 56, where you state, Professor --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it possible that you misspoke? Instead of P303 it should be P3003.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P3003. I apologise to the interpreters. I speak too fast. So that would be P3003 at paragraph 56. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Here, you state, Professor, in such context of events - that would be paragraph 56, second sentence: [As read] "Following a controversial session of the SRBiH Assembly on the 14th and 15th of October, on expanded meeting of the SDS party council - in fact, the political council - was held on the 15th of October. It was attended, inter alia, by Karadzic as president of the SDS, Serbian members of the Presidency and government of SRBiH, and members of the Executive Board ... Bosnian Serb leaders present - prominent among them Karadzic, Krajisnik, Plavsic, and Koljevic reacted strongly to the SRBiH Assembly's vote for Bosnian sovereignty ..." My question to you, Professor, is this: Why did you qualify that assembly as controversial?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, because the -- the decisions taken there were -- as we've seen in some of the articles of the -- the constitution of the SFRY, that you've enumerated and indeed the constitution of the SRBiH decisions which were -- could be viewed as in contravention with that, and of course the decisions were strongly opposed by especially the Serbian members of the assembly. The decisions were not a total surprise, however, to -- to anybody. There had been much discussion of the whole issue of the -- the future of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the -- in the weeks preceding, especially after the declaration of independence of Slovenia and Croatia. And I believe drafts of this -- of these -- of the two controversial decisions had been circulated previously. So they knew what was in the offing, but of course when it happened, then they -- the Bosnian Serbs were ready to react.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I'm looking at the clock. It's time for a break. It wasn't entirely clear to me with the last question whether you wanted to challenge what the witness wrote, that is to say, that the Defence takes issue with this is controversial or do you think it's not controversial, and whether there is any disagreement about it? Is it your position -- is it the Defence's position that it was not controversial, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not, Your Honour. This could be a semantic issue, whether it's controversial or not. But the gist Defence is the reply we received; to wit, decision of that session of the assembly contravened both constitution of the SRBiH and SFRY, and later on we are going do deal with the nature of those decisions, whether they are controversial or contravening the interests of a constituent nation is what you, history, and everybody living in Bosnia-Herzegovina will have to take a decision on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you should further explore that, because I did not hear the witness say that a decision contravened both constitution of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the SFRY. I didn't hear but perhaps I missed something, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I did say, Your Honour, that the -- the decisions taken at that session could be viewed as contravening both of those constitutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the controversy, controversy --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But -- or did you express as your opinion that they were -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I'm hesitant to may -- advance any legal opinion, but they certainly were viewed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's my -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- by political actors at the time and among the general people as -- in -- possibly in contravention of those two constitutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not trying to elicit from you a legal opinion on the matter. We take a break, and we'll resume after the witness has left the courtroom. We'll then take a break of 20 minutes and resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
